title: Constant-sheaf comparison for the ring lift
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ and $(C',J')$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in a common universe, and let
$L:\operatorname{Sh}(C,J,\mathrm{Set})\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Sh}(C',J',\mathrm{Set}):V$ be an adjunction
whose left adjoint preserves finite limits. Write $|{-}|$ for underlying sheaves of sets of ring sheaves
[def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\operatorname{rings}:\operatorname{Sh}(C,J,\mathrm{CommRing})\to\operatorname{Sh}(C',J',\mathrm{CommRing})$
be a functor and $e_R:L(|R|)\simeq|\operatorname{rings}(R)|$ isomorphisms, natural in ring-sheaf morphisms $R\to S$, such that each $e_R$
carries $L$ of the addition, multiplication, zero and one of $R$ (composed with the inverse canonical finite-product and
terminal comparisons of $L$) to those of $\operatorname{rings}(R)$. For the constant commutative-ring sheaf functors
$\underline{(-)}_C$ and $\underline{(-)}_{C'}$ defined in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], there is a natural
isomorphism
$\operatorname{constants}:\underline{(-)}_C\,;\,\operatorname{rings}\simeq\underline{(-)}_{C'}$ of functors from commutative rings
to ring sheaves on $(C',J')$. For every commutative ring $A$, the underlying map of sheaves of sets of its component is
$e_{\underline A_C}^{-1}$ followed by the canonical comparison $L(\underline A_C)\simeq\underline A_{C'}$ obtained by writing the constant
sheaf of the set $A$ as the coproduct of $A$ copies of the terminal sheaf (the injections being the sheafified constant sections)
and using that $L$ preserves the terminal sheaf and coproducts; the components commute with every ring homomorphism $A\to B$.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: For a set E and a sheaf of sets H on (C,J), a map of presheaves from the constant presheaf U ↦ E to H is the same as a family, indexed by e in E, of maps from the constant singleton presheaf to H; the constant singleton presheaf is the terminal sheaf 1_C, so such a map is one global section of H for each e. By the sheafification universal property of the constant sheaf, maps underline E_C → H are therefore exactly such E-indexed families, the family of a map being its composites with the constant-section injections i_e:1_C → underline E_C. Hence (underline E_C,(i_e)_e) is itself a coproduct C_E of E copies of the terminal sheaf (also for E empty, where it is the initial sheaf), and we write j_e=i_e for its coprojections. Uniqueness of maps out of a coproduct shows that for a map of sets a:E→F the sheaf map underline a satisfies underline a ∘ i_e = i_{a(e)}.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf), together with the sheafification universal property

proof.text: Because L is a left adjoint, [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] applied to the discrete E-indexed coproduct (underline E_C,(i_e)_e) of Step 1 shows that (L(underline E_C),(L i_e)_e) is a coproduct of the objects L(1_C) in Sh(C',J',Set). The finite-limit hypothesis (the empty limit) gives the canonical terminal comparison t:L(1_C) ≅ 1_{C'}. By Step 1 on (C',J'), (underline E_{C'},(i'_e)_e) is a coproduct of E copies of 1_{C'}. Hence there is a unique morphism kappa_E:L(underline E_C) → underline E_{C'} with kappa_E ∘ L(i_e) = i'_e ∘ t for every e, and it is an isomorphism (both sides are coproducts of isomorphic families). For a map of sets a:E→F, the two maps kappa_F ∘ L(underline a) and underline a ∘ kappa_E agree after every L(i_e), by the equations underline a ∘ i_e = i_{a(e)} of Step 1 on both sites, so they are equal: kappa is natural in maps of sets.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (constant sheaf) and the adjunction-colimit property used in the construction sentence

proof.text: For a commutative ring A, set c_A=e_{underline A_C}^{-1} followed by kappa_|A|. Two identifications are used. First, by [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] (commutative-ring case), the underlying sheaf of sets of the constant commutative-ring sheaf underline A_C is the set-valued sheafification of the constant presheaf |A|, i.e. the constant sheaf of the set |A|, with the same constant sections i_a; its addition and multiplication are the sheafifications of the constant presheaf maps, so they send the pair (i_a,i_b) to i_{a+b}, resp. i_{ab}, and zero and one are i_0, i_1. Second, by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] sheafification of presheaves of sets preserves finite products and the terminal object, so the product of the constant set sheaves of |A| with itself is the constant sheaf of |A|×|A|, its section i_{(a,b)} having projections i_a and i_b; the same holds on (C',J'). Now compare kappa_|A| ∘ L(+) with +' ∘ (kappa_|A| × kappa_|A|) ∘ (product comparison of L) as maps out of L(underline A_C × underline A_C): by naturality of kappa (Step 2) for the two projections |A|×|A|→|A| and for the addition map |A|×|A|→|A|, both composites restricted along L(i_{(a,b)}) equal i'_{a+b} after the terminal comparison L(1_C) ≅ 1_{C'}, for every pair (a,b). Since (L(underline{|A|×|A|}_C),(L i_{(a,b)})) is a coproduct (Step 2), the composites are equal. Multiplication is the same with ab, and zero and one are the singleton-set maps selecting 0 and 1. The assumed operation equations for e identify e^{-1} with the inverse of the transported ring structure, so these equalities say that the set-sheaf map c_A commutes with addition, multiplication, zero and one; a map of sheaves of commutative rings is a map of underlying sheaves of sets that does, so c_A is a ring-sheaf morphism, and it is an isomorphism because e and kappa are isomorphisms.

If f:A→B is a ring homomorphism, the square for c_A and c_B commutes: e-naturality gives the square for e^{-1} applied to the ring-sheaf map underline f_C; under the identification of Step 3 [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], the underlying set map of underline f_C (resp. underline f_{C'}) is a ring-sheaf map that sends each constant section i_a to i_{f(a)}, hence is the set-sheaf map underline |f| of Step 1, and Step 2 gives the square for kappa_|f|. Thus the c_A assemble to a natural isomorphism constants from the constant ring-sheaf functor on C followed by rings to the constant ring-sheaf functor on C'. By construction its underlying component is exactly e_{underline A_C}^{-1} followed by the canonical kappa_|A|, and the argument includes the empty set and zero ring cases.

split_report.summary: Audited the abstract constant-ring comparison statement against Tags 0H7J and 00YV. No new node was needed: the constant sheaf as the coproduct of copies of the terminal sheaf follows directly from the sheafification universal property, while preservation of that coproduct is the existing left-adjoint-colimits leaf. The proof constructs the set-level comparison, checks ring operations by coprojection restrictions and the assumed operation equations for e_R, and checks naturality in ring maps.
split_report.blueprint: The four steps realize the sk-thm-rationality construction sentence: the left adjoint preserves coproducts of the terminal sheaf and therefore gives the natural constant-sheaf comparison.

tool_uses.why: Step 2 needs the generic theorem that the given left adjoint preserves the indexed coproduct used to express the constant sheaf; no node in sk-thm-rationality states this category-theoretic fact.
